text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000027 bills 99215 at roughly twice the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including on patients with no chronic conditions, but too few charts came back to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not explained by a sicker panel. The 99215 share runs about double the all-provider share in every condition band, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s include visits with no chronic conditions coded only for upper respiratory infection, UTI, rash or follow-up (e.g., C0013170, C0013418, C0013154, C0014034), which is a pattern consistent with upcoding; the heavy concentration of 99214 in the mix points the same way. Against that, all four documented 99215s were supported, including three on single-condition patients (C0013071, C0013117, C0013296) documented at high MDM. But four charts out of 181 99215 claims is too thin to judge, and high MDM on a single-condition diabetes or depression visit is itself worth checking for templated or inflated notes, as are the 3 notes that claim moderate-plus data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim. A reviewer should first request records targeted at the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet and compare note content across visits for cloned language, then extend the request to a sample of 99214s."}
